title: RWB-E2-008: the seven consumed operation names and payloads are not published, and the plan C row names four P3 contracts only
source: Template and Rules v1 R5.4, R5.5, R7 and R9; split_plan slice RWB-P8-E2008-APP (H, C, I, X); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 17, 41 and 44; TSD P8 Payments and posting v2 T5.2, T6.1, T-A.1 and T-A.2; FSD P8 Payments and posting v3 A2.1 and A2.2; legacy RWB-E2-008 section 12
description: (1) The legacy story calls six published interfaces in process: RuleEvaluator.evaluate, RecoveryDataApi.paymentsLoaded, CaseWorkflowApi.openCaseForAccount, TreatmentApi.runningPlans, TreatmentApi.recordInstallmentPaid, RecoveryDataApi.nextInstallmentDate and BatchStatusQuery.forSource. Under D-RCV-60 each becomes a one-hop REST contract of its owner (DP-11) and no source publishes an operation name or a payload for any of them. (2) The plan C row names RWB-P3-E1042-CON, RWB-P3-E1043-CON, RWB-P3-E2004-CON and RWB-P3-E2042-CON, while the build also needs the rwb-source-data payments, next-installment and batch-status rows, the rwb-case open-case row, the treatment record read and update, and the rwb-decision package read, and DP-04 adds C RWB-P7-E1073-CON which the plan C row does not carry. (3) The plan scopes the treatment record of legacy RWB-E2-004 as RWB-P3-E2004-CON and the rule-package surface as RWB-P3-E2042-CON, while Architecture v5 slides 18 and 41 and the Ownership Map give the live treatment records to S2 rwb-treatment and the rule registry to P7 rwb-decision, so the scope of two C rows is read in two ways and no source names the operations behind them. (4) The service reads the three ACE products through v_ace_payment, v_ace_account and v_ace_batch_status; whether the row is the rwb-source-data contract or the service own read-only views is not fixed for this key.
evidence: legacy RWB-E2-008 section 12 code block and its Published interfaces called heading; split_plan slice RWB-P8-E2008-APP with C of four P3 contracts and empty I; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 rows DP-04, DP-05 and DP-11; Architecture v5 slide 17 IN and OUT for P8; Architecture v5 slides 18, 29, 37, 41 and 45; ownership.json api rows for GET /proceeds and POST /proceeds/{proceedsId}/match and tables row for proceeds (owner P8); TSD P8 v2 T5.2 and T-A.1
area: Consumed contracts, dependency rows and ownership of the treatment record
proposed: Keep the plan H, C, I and X rows exactly as given, name the seven consumed rows in section 12.2 with the placeholder until each owner publishes its operation, build against their fakes on Day 1, and ask the solution architect to confirm the scope of RWB-P3-E2004-CON, RWB-P3-E2042-CON and RWB-P7-E1073-CON

title: RWB-E2-008: the three event payloads and the decision-record element are not fixed by any source
source: Template and Rules v1 R5.5 and R7.2 s12; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 17, slide 42 rows 08, 11 and 12, slide 43 row 25 and the slide 42 notes; TSD P8 Payments and posting v2 T5.3; legacy RWB-E2-008 sections 12 and 13
description: Architecture v5 slide 17 OUT gives the topic rwb.payment.events.v1 three events, TreatmentBooked, PaymentMissed and ProceedsMatched, and the two catalogues give their consumers, their topic and the CloudEvents envelope with key caseId, but no source gives the data element of any of the three. The legacy story names three fields for PaymentMissed (treatmentId, dueDate, amountDue) and three for ProceedsMatched (proceedsId, caseId, amount), and names no field at all for TreatmentBooked. The local decision record of DP-03 replaces the central decision log and the legacy story names a decision code, a rule id and a rule version but no other element, while the record element itself is the library of RWB-PLT-E1027-CON. DecisionRecorded (EV-08) is produced by all 19 services on the shared topic rwb.decision-record.v1 whose owner is P7, so its schema is named by this service and owned by another.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 17 OUT line and slide 42 notes (events carry IDs and facts, never personal data; schemas versioned in the registry with BACKWARD compatibility); slide 42 rows 08, 11 and 12 and slide 43 row 25; TSD P8 v2 T5.3 with the three directions only; legacy RWB-E2-008 section 12 Events published row and section 13 build step 6; ownership.json events rows EV-08, EV-11, EV-12 and EV-25
proposed: Publish the three event schemas through RWB-P8-E2008-CON with the three data fields the legacy story names per event and the CloudEvents envelope of the platform library, keep the decision-record element with its library owner, and require a new schema version for any added business field

title: RWB-E2-008: the proceeds field set and its idempotency tables disagree between the legacy story and TSD P8 T3.1
source: Template and Rules v1 R3 (R-PREC) and R5.5 DP-01 and DP-15; TSD P8 Payments and posting v2 T3.1 and T3.3 and Appendix T-B; legacy RWB-E2-008 sections 11 and 13; Ownership Map tables row proceeds (owner P8)
description: The legacy story keys a proceeds row on payment_code and asks for the unique index ux_proceeds_payment_code on it, and asks for a second table payment_missed_event_key with a unique key on treatment_id and due_date for the event idempotency. TSD P8 T3.1 gives the table nine fields DF-FIN-001 to DF-FIN-009 with account_payment_id (DF-FIN-004) and no payment_code, and no payment_missed_event_key table; Physical Schema v6 counts 93 tables and carries no such table. The legacy story also names the migration V2_008__payment_matching.sql, which is a number of the monolith sequence and not of this service own sequence. By R-PREC the TSD outranks the story master, so the field set and the table list of the TSD win and the legacy key names are left without a home.
evidence: legacy RWB-E2-008 section 11 rows DF-FIN-001 to DF-FIN-009 and DF-FIN-004 payment_code, and section 13 Database bullet with ux_proceeds_payment_code and payment_missed_event_key; TSD P8 v2 T3.1 proceeds table with account_payment_id and nine fields, T3.3 relationships, Appendix T-B; Physical Schema v6 table count in legacy section 13; Template and Rules v1 R3 source order
area: Owned table field set and migration naming
proposed: Keep the TSD P8 T3.1 field set for proceeds, hold the payment identity on account_payment_id where the owner supplies it, replace payment_missed_event_key with the platform idempotency_key table of DP-09, take the next number of the service own Flyway sequence, and ask the data owner to confirm where the payment code is held

title: RWB-E2-008: the case payment read, the SCR-28 and run-view field lists and the activity names of JOB-07 are not fixed by any source
source: Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-10 and DP-19 and R7.2 s15; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 17 and 44; FSD P8 Payments and posting v3 Screens table; TSD P8 Payments and posting v2 T-A.1; legacy RWB-E2-008 sections 13 and 15; ownership.json api and jobs rows
description: (1) Architecture v5 slide 17 lists GET /cases/{id}/payments among the IN operations of rwb-payment while the Ownership Map carries no row for it and the two published operations are GET /proceeds and POST /proceeds/{proceedsId}/match, so the case payment read has no published home. (2) FSD P8 names SCR-28 Proceeds matching as an E2 skeleton and SCR-29 Posting for E4 and gives no field list; the legacy story gives the SCR-28 states Loading, matched and unmatched and describes SCR-44 as the JOB-07 run summary, while under DP-10 there is no job monitor and the run is a workflow execution. No source names the run-view fields of an event-started workflow. (3) The gateway-bff composite route specification and the screen field lists belong to RWB-PLT-N001-CON and are not published. (4) No source names the step activities of JOB-07: Architecture v5 slide 17 names Act: matchPayments, confirmBookings and postProceeds as activities of the service and ownership.json names matchPayments as the replacement of JOB-07, so the workflow and its step activities carry one name between them.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 17 IN line and OUT line and slide 44 row JOB-07; FSD P8 v3 Screens table rows SCR-28 and SCR-29; legacy RWB-E2-008 section 15 and section 13 component table; TSD P8 v2 T-A.1 with the two operations only; ownership.json api rows and jobs row JOB-07
area: Read surface, screens and workflow decomposition
proposed: Answer the case payment list through GET /proceeds with the case scope applied and publish no extra operation, read the SCR-28 field list and the run view from the edge contract, name the workflow matchPayments and the four step activities as the design choice of the story, and leave the screen field lists with RWB-PLT-N001-CON

title: RWB-E2-008: the contract artefact names, the problem+json body, the MatchRequest shape and the registry mode of rwb-payment are not fixed by any source
source: Template and Rules v1 R5.4, R7.2 s12 and R9; TSD P8 Payments and posting v2 T-A.1 and T-A.2 and Appendix T-B; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 17 tags and slide 42 notes; Ownership Map api rows
description: TSD P8 T-A.2 names the two operations, their access, the Idempotency-Key header and the status codes 401, 403, 404, 409, 422 and 503, and names neither the document artefact nor the error body schema nor the properties of MatchRequest. Architecture v5 slide 42 notes fix the registry compatibility as BACKWARD for every event schema but name no registry artefact and no compatibility setting for a REST document. The service base, the schema, the topic and the queue are fixed by section R4 and Architecture v5 slide 41; the document file name, the AsyncAPI artefact name, the problem+json member set, the MatchRequest properties, the migration number of the baseline and the versioning rule of a breaking REST change have no source.
evidence: TSD P8 v2 T-A.1 endpoint inventory and T-A.2 API-P8-001 and API-P8-002 detail rows; Architecture v5 slide 42 notes on registry versioning; Architecture v5 slide 17 tags line (REST = OpenAPI 3.1, EVT = Kafka topic with CloudEvents and AsyncAPI); ownership.json api rows; Template and Rules v1 R4 naming
area: Contract artefacts, error model and versioning
proposed: Publish one OpenAPI 3.1 document and one AsyncAPI document per service, a problem+json body on every non-2xx status, a MatchRequest of the proceeds identifier, the case, the treatment, the account payment and a reason code, the next number of the service own Flyway sequence, and major version 1 with BACKWARD acceptance

title: RWB-E2-008: the producer and the owner of DecisionRecorded disagree between the event catalogue and the messaging design
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 42 row 08 and slide 20; ownership.json events row EV-08 with its ruling; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-03; TSD P8 Payments and posting v2 T5.3
description: Architecture v5 slide 42 row 08 gives DecisionRecorded the producer all 19 services on the shared topic rwb.decision-record.v1 and the consumers rwb-decision and rwb-reporting, while Event and Messaging Design v4 names the owning module Decision center and log. TSD P8 T5.3 lists only TreatmentBooked, PaymentMissed and ProceedsMatched for this module and does not name the record event at all. The contract of rwb-payment must therefore name a record event that it produces but does not own, with a schema that its own AsyncAPI document cannot declare, and must say which of the two documents a consumer builds its fake against.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 42 row 08 producer all 19 and consumers rwb-decision and rwb-reporting; slide 20 ledger in rwb-decision; ownership.json events row EV-08 with its ruling and its ASM; TSD P8 v2 T5.3 three events only; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-03
area: Decision-record event ownership and schema home
proposed: Keep the record event with rwb-decision as the owner of the topic and the central ledger, name it in the service AsyncAPI document as a produced event whose schema is the owner's, and have the service publish it only through the local library of DP-03

title: RWB-E2-008: the deployment targets, the tier sizes, the rollout strategy and the rollback procedure of rwb-payment have no source
source: Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-01, DP-09, DP-10 and DP-15; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 20, 29, 33, 41, 44 and 48; TSD P8 Payments and posting v2 T6, T7 and Appendix T-B; NFR-052, NFR-053 and NFR-054
description: Architecture v5 slides 33 and 48 fix two api copies and a worker tier that KEDA scales on the service own queue, slide 20 fixes /health and /metrics and one schema and login per service, and slide 44 fixes JOB-07 as an event-started workflow. No source fixes the worker replica floor and ceiling of this service, the resource requests and limits of either tier, the cluster and the environment names, the partition count and the retention of the three topics, the subscription set beyond the consumed rows, the rollout strategy of PROD, the release gate approvers, the rollback window and the procedure that restores a schema version after a forward migration. TSD P8 Appendix T-B records DL35 Deployment slots and DL11 Non-functional target values as open decisions.
evidence: Architecture v5 slides 20, 29, 33, 41, 44 and 48; TSD P8 v2 T6.2, T7 and Appendix T-B rows DL06, DL11 and DL35; NFR-052, NFR-053 and NFR-054; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-09, DP-10 and DP-15
area: Deployment unit, topics, worker pool and release process
proposed: Render the unit from the pinned chart with two api replicas and a worker tier whose floor, ceiling and sizes are values, create the three topics with the platform partition and retention defaults, gate every environment, take a canary or a blue/green step for PROD and require a down script per migration for the rollback

title: RWB-E2-008: no source fixes a numeric target for the outbox-lag, dead-letter or workflow-failure alerts of rwb-payment
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 42 notes and slide 44 notes; TSD P8 Payments and posting v2 T7 and Appendix T-B row DL11; NFR-052 to NFR-056; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-09 and DP-10
description: The three operative failure modes that the event-started replacement of JOB-07 introduces are an outbox row that never reaches the topic, a poison event that loops in rwb.payment.events.v1.retry and a workflow that fails after its last attempt. No source gives an age, a depth, a count or a window for any of them: TSD P8 T7 carries no availability, latency or throughput target and marks DL11 Non-functional target values as open, and Architecture v5 gives the mechanism of the relay and the workflow without a measurement. The alert thresholds, the API error-rate and latency thresholds and the canary gate thresholds of this service are therefore values in force with no source behind them.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 42 notes on the outbox relay and slide 44 notes on the event-triggered workflow; TSD P8 v2 T7 rows NFR-049 to NFR-056 without a numeric target and Appendix T-B row DL11; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-09 and DP-10; legacy RWB-E2-008 has no non-functional row
proposed: Hold every threshold as data in the service values file with no default that reads as a target, raise the three alerts on their own measurement, and close the gap with the solution architect and the platform administrator before the PROD release

title: Legacy AC1, AC3, AC4 and AC5 of RWB-E2-008 are owned by no story in this split

evidence: WP B-P8-01 story line RWB-P8-E2008-APP: "acs": ["AC2", "AC6", "AC7", "AC8", "AC9"]
proposed: Reallocate AC1, AC3, AC4 and AC5 to RWB-P8-E2008-APP in the next revision of the split plan, or add a coverage note to the epic overview.

title: The AC6 package load and the rule-evaluation contract have no C row in this key
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 2 Story Files v5/RWB E2 027 Payment matching rules with the data team v2.md sections 7 and 12; _work/msr/plan/ownership.json rows rule_package, rule_package_version and rule_row; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1.md R5.5 DP-04
description: The legacy AC6 loads a package version through POST /api/recovery/v1/admin/rule-packages/PAYMENT_MATCH/versions and its checks are the registry of rwb-decision (P7). DP-04 adds C RWB-P7-E1073-CON and the registry story is RWB-P7-E2027-APP, but the metadata C row of this key carries only the three rwb-case contracts. The legacy path is also the monolith base and not the target base /api/recovery/decision/v1.
evidence: Legacy AC6 When step and legacy section 12 name the monolith path; ownership.json gives P7 the four registry tables; Template and Rules R5.5 DP-04 row
proposed: Read AC6 through the rwb-decision contract mock, keep every legacy step verbatim, and add C RWB-P7-E1073-CON to the C row of RWB-P8-E2027-APP in D1.

title: The ordering column is called row order in the story and priority in the TSD
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 2 Story Files v5/RWB E2 027 Payment matching rules with the data team v2.md sections 7 and 11; _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P8 Payments and posting v2.md T3.1; _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD P8 Payments and posting v3.md A2.1.4.3
section: 7. Acceptance criteria AC6; 8. Business rules; 11. Data
description: The legacy story, its standalone Background and the target read the ordering of the PAYMENT_MATCH rows as row order, while TSD P8 v2 T3.1 names the column priority (DF-REF-270) and FSD AC-EXC-P8-001-07 says priority 2 for the same invalid version. One column needs one name for the rule rows, the load check and the evaluation result.
evidence: Legacy AC6 Given names row order 2; TSD P8 T3.1 field DF-REF-270 is priority; FSD AC-EXC-P8-001-07 says both rows have priority 2
proposed: Keep row order as the target name of the column, record priority as its legacy and TSD name, and have rwb-decision publish the one name in the rule_row catalogue and in the evaluation result.

title: The PAYMENT_MATCH version label differs between RWB-E2-027 and RWB-E2-042
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 2 Story Files v5/RWB E2 027 Payment matching rules with the data team v2.md sections 3 and 7; 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Service Story Files v1/RWB-SVC-P3 rwb-case (Case and workflow)/RWB P3 E2042 OPS Epic 2 rule packages in Drools - deployment v1.md section 3
description: RWB-E2-027 puts version PM-2026.12 in force from 2026-12-01, while the rwb-case story of the same package code uses the label PMT-2026.12 from 2026-12-15. Two labels for one package would put two versions in force and every match would name an ambiguous version.
evidence: Legacy Background and precondition give PM-2026.12 from 2026-12-01; RWB-P3-E2042-OPS precondition lists PAYMENT_MATCH PMT-2026.12
proposed: Read PM-2026.12 as the single version in force for this key and reconcile the PMT-2026.12 label to one version row in rwb-decision before SIT.

title: DecisionRecorded is listed as consumed here but the catalogue names only two consumers
source: 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md slide 42 row 08; service conventions of WP B-P8-01
description: Arch v5 slide 42 row 08 lists rwb-decision and rwb-reporting as the consumers of DecisionRecorded on rwb.decision-record.v1, while the service conventions of this WP list it among the consumed events of rwb-payment. The record itself is written locally by the library, so a second consumer registration would duplicate the ledger read for no business need.
evidence: Arch v5 slide 42 row 08 consumers rwb-decision and rwb-reporting; the WP service convention lists DecisionRecorded among the consumed events
proposed: Declare DecisionRecorded as read only for the ledger acknowledgement of a local record, register no second writer, and confirm the consumer list with the event catalogue owner.

title: The rule-evaluation result has no published schema and two of its field names are not given
source: 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1.md slide 14 notes 4 to 6 and slide 16; 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 2 Story Files v5/RWB E2 027 Payment matching rules with the data team v2.md section 12
section: 7. Acceptance criteria AC1; 12.2 REST operations consumed
description: The Temporal and Drools design names RuleResult(packageCode, packageVersion, ruleId, outputs) and the legacy story names RuleEvaluator.evaluate, and no source publishes a schema or a row-order field. The operation names of the version-in-force lookup and of the treatment installment-paid call are not given either, so the consumed contract of AC1 carries placeholders.
evidence: Temporal and Drools slide 14 notes 4 to 6 and slide 16 RuleResult block; legacy section 12 published interfaces; no OpenAPI or AsyncAPI document for rwb-decision in the read set
proposed: Publish the result as packageCode, versionInForce, ruleId, rowOrder and outputs in RWB-P8-E2027-CON, mark the two names as placeholders, and have rwb-decision confirm them in RWB-P7-E1073-CON.

title: The three payment event payloads have no schema in any source
source: _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P8 Payments and posting v2.md T5.3; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md slides 17, 42 and 43
description: TSD P8 v2 T5.3 gives the three event names and their direction only, and the Arch v5 catalogue gives producer, topic and consumers and no payload. The payload field lists published in RWB-P8-E2027-CON are therefore derived from the legacy facts and are marked.
evidence: TSD P8 T5.3 table of TreatmentBooked, PaymentMissed and ProceedsMatched; Arch v5 slide 42 rows 11 and 12 and slide 43 row 25 carry no payload
proposed: Publish the payload field lists of the three events in the AsyncAPI fragment of RWB-P8-E2027-CON as the working read, identifiers and facts only, and confirm them with the consumers named in the catalogue.

title: No numeric operations value is specified for the matching service
source: _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P8 Payments and posting v2.md T7 and appendix T-B; 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Service Story Files v1/RWB-SVC-P3 rwb-case (Case and workflow)/RWB P3 E2042 OPS Epic 2 rule packages in Drools - deployment v1.md section 11
section: 7. Acceptance criteria AC6; 11. Data; 13. Solution plan

TSD P8 T7 carries qualitative NFRs and appendix T-B leaves DL11 open on the non-functional target values.
evidence: TSD P8 T7 rows NFR-049 to NFR-056 carry no threshold; TSD P8 appendix T-B lists DL11 non-functional target values as open
proposed: Expose every value as a chart value with a placeholder in the three values files and close them with the DL11 decisions before UAT.

title: The secret names, the workload identity and the certificate of rwb-payment are not specified
source: _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P8 Payments and posting v2.md T6.2 and T7 NFR-052; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1.md R5.5 DP-02
description: The per-service login, the Kafka client credential, the Temporal mTLS material and the registry certificate are required by the deployment, but no source names them or the workload identity. TSD P8 T6.2 names only Entra ID single sign-on and service identities in general.
evidence: TSD P8 T6.2 authentication paragraph; NFR-052 requires secrets in the key store with no name; no platform secret-store catalogue in the read set
proposed: Reference every secret and the workload identity by role in the chart, record the names in the platform secret-store catalogue, and keep the phrase the rwb-payment login (DP-02).

title: Legacy RWB-E4-043 acceptance criteria and test cases are generic placeholders
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md, heading RWB-E4-043
description: Legacy AC1 states only that the data and the rule version this feature needs are in place and that its trigger arrives; legacy AC2 states only that the action is taken; TC-E4-043-01 to TC-E4-043-04 carry no settlement-specific data. No legacy value names the trigger, the settlement outcome fields or the fixture data, so the settlement detail is taken from FSD P8 A2.3 and TSD P8 and every value no source gives carries the placeholder.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E4-043: 'Given the data and the rule version this feature needs are in place / When its trigger arrives'; legacy test case table rows TC-E4-043-01, TC-E4-043-02, TC-E4-043-03 (AC access) and TC-E4-043-04 (Principle 5).
proposed: Keep the two legacy criteria word for word in RWB-P8-E4043-APP with their origin tag, fill the settlement detail from FSD P8 A2.3 and TSD P8, and cite FEAT-PAY-03 with AC-P8-003-01 in place of a requirement id, which the split plan does not carry for this slice.

title: Settlement match outcomes, rule package code, thresholds and money-side close state have no source value
source: TSD P8 Payments and posting v2 T3.1, T3.2 and T-A; FSD P8 Payments and posting v3 A2.3; Temporal and Drools Design slide 18
section: Business rules, data and state transitions
description: The TSD gives the columns of proceeds (DF-FIN-001 to DF-FIN-009) and of payment_match_rule with no row values, and two lists; the FSD gives only BR-P8-003 and VR-P8-003-1 and one main success criterion. No source names the outcome fields the settlement arm writes, the package code or rule IDs of the match itself, the amount tolerance, the matching window or the state name of the money-side close, so the proceeds row carries matched_to SETTLEMENT and every other value is held as a rule row or reference data with the placeholder.
evidence: TSD P8 T3.1 lists columns and sources only, with amount_tolerance_pct, window_days_before, window_days_after, grace_days and partial_floor_pct carrying no value; TSD P8 T3.2 lists LOV-MATCH and LOV-PROCEEDS-SRC only; FSD P8 A2.3.3.1 has one business rule and one validation rule; Temporal and Drools Design slide 18 names PAYMENT_MATCH as replacing payment_match_rule without a rule list.
proposed: Hold the outcome fields, thresholds, tolerance, window and close state as rule rows and reference data governed in rwb-decision, write only matched_to SETTLEMENT and the references in rwb_payment.proceeds, and never write a value in code.

title: The legacy step reads v_ace_payment and four other modules tables in process
source: Legacy RWB-E4-043 data table; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 29 and slide 41
description: The legacy data table reads v_ace_payment (DF-ACE-043 to DF-ACE-054) and the treatment, recovery_case, decision_log_entry and rule_row tables in the same process. Architecture v5 slide 29 gives SELECT on the recovery.v_ace_* views to rwb_source_data only and no grant across rwb_* schemas, and the Ownership Map places treatment with S2, recovery_case with P3 and the rule tables with P7, so every fact is consumed on its owner contract and the ACE view is never read here.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E4-043 Data table rows v_ace_payment, treatment, recovery_case, decision_log_entry and rule_row; Architecture v5 slide 29 notes ('only rwb_source_data has SELECT on the views; no cross-schema joins, views or foreign keys').
proposed: Apply DP-05 as a prohibition: read the receipt on the rwb-source-data contract, the treatment on GET /treatments/{treatmentId} of S2, the case on the rwb-case contract, and write the decision record locally through RWB-PLT-E1027-CON.

title: The field lists of MatchRequest, ProceedsPage and the remaining Proceeds answer are not specified
source: TSD P8 Payments and posting v2 T-A.2 (API-P8-001 and API-P8-002)
description: The TSD names MatchRequest, ProceedsPage and Proceeds as the request and answer elements and gives the query parameters matched, from, to, page and size, but publishes no field list for any of the three. The nine columns of proceeds fix the Proceeds element only in part, and the request element has no published source at all, so the document is written from those columns and parameters and every field with no source carries the placeholder.
evidence: TSD P8 T-A.2: 'Request MatchRequest; Response Proceeds' for API-P8-002 and 'Request Query: matched, from, to, page, size; Response ProceedsPage' for API-P8-001, with no element tables.
proposed: Declare Proceeds on DF-FIN-001 to DF-FIN-009, ProceedsPage on the platform pagination convention and MatchRequest on the fields the match needs, and mark every unstated field with the placeholder in the document and in its fakes.

title: The payloads of TreatmentBooked and ProceedsMatched are not published
source: Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 22, 42 and 43; TSD P8 Payments and posting v2 T5.3
description: The catalogue names the three events of rwb-payment with their topic and consumers, and slide 22 publishes a full PaymentMissed example with caseId, treatmentId, dueDate, amountDue and daysLate; no source publishes a payload for TreatmentBooked or for ProceedsMatched, and no source fixes the field list of the match fact the five consumers of ProceedsMatched receive. The two schemas are therefore written from the modelled columns of proceeds and treatment, the envelope of slide 22 and the rule that events carry IDs and facts only.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 42 rows 11 and 12 and slide 43 row 25 (names, topic and consumers only); slide 22 payload example for PaymentMissed only; TSD P8 T5.3 (event names and direction only).
proposed: Declare the two schemas on the identifiers and facts of the modelled rows with the CloudEvents envelope of slide 22, and mark every unstated field with the placeholder until the consumers and the owner confirm the field list.

title: No rule row, package code or rule ID exists for the settlement arm of the match
source: FSD P8 Payments and posting v3 A2.3.3.1; Temporal and Drools Design slide 18; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4
description: The settlement arm of the match has no rule row in the routing logic: R-SET-13 sets the payment due date, R-SET-21 closes the case on the collateral release and R-SET-23 and R-SET-24 handle a reversal, and none of them matches a settlement receipt. The FSD gives only BR-P8-003 and VR-P8-003-1, and the Temporal and Drools design names PAYMENT_MATCH as replacing payment_match_rule without a package code or a rule list. The contract therefore names the package and fixes no rule ID.
evidence: Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 has no payment-matching rule row for settlement; FSD P8 A2.3.3.1 has one business rule and one validation rule; Temporal and Drools Design slide 18 note 'PAYMENT_MATCH replaces payment_match_rule (T10)'.
proposed: Govern the settlement arm as rules of the PAYMENT_MATCH package in rwb-decision, name the package in the contract without a rule ID, and leave the rule IDs and outputs to the package authoring and approval story.

title: Legacy acceptance criteria and test cases of RWB-E4-044 are generic placeholders
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md, heading RWB-E4-044; FSD P8 Payments and posting v3 A2.4.4
section: A2.4.4 Acceptance criteria; legacy Acceptance criteria and Test cases
description: The two legacy acceptance criteria and the four legacy test cases of RWB-E4-044 are written in generic wording and name no field, amount, threshold, operation or screen state; the FSD main success row of AC-P8-004-01 is equally generic and defers to a story written one epic ahead.
evidence: Legacy AC1: Given the data and the rule version this feature needs are in place / When its trigger arrives. Legacy AC2: Given the decision log cannot be written. FSD P8 A2.4.4.1 AC-P8-004-01 story column: Written one epic ahead.
proposed: Read the criteria against FSD P8 A2.4 VR-P8-004-1 and BR-P8-004 and TSD P8 API-P8-001 and API-P8-002, keep the legacy lines word for word with the origin tag, and add only one mocked Given per criterion for the cross-service part.

title: Contract dependencies row is None while the match reads five other services
source: _work/msr/plan/split_plan.json RWB-P8-E4044-APP; TSD P8 Payments and posting v2 T-A
section: Metadata, Contract dependencies; s12.2 REST operations consumed
description: The split plan sets the contract dependencies of this slice to None, yet the match needs the rwb-source-data payment data product, the rwb-case reference-data and case-state reads, the rwb-decision rule package and the rwb-integration posting file, each one hop with a 2 s budget.
evidence: split_plan.json RWB-P8-E4044-APP has C empty; TSD P8 T5.1 and T5.2 name the core bank, GL and cross-module reads; Architecture v5 slide 17 gives rwb-payment the payment matching on source data.
proposed: Treat the five rows as class C dependencies, build against their published documents and fakes on Day 1, and leave the plan row unchanged until the assembler renumbers the registers.

title: The elements of MatchRequest are not published
source: TSD P8 Payments and posting v2 T-A.2 API-P8-002
description: API-P8-002 names the request as MatchRequest and gives no element list, and the legacy endpoints table names the path only, so the request the officer sends to match a receipt to a case is not specified in any source.
evidence: TSD P8 T-A.2 API-P8-002: Request MatchRequest, Response Proceeds, Errors 401, 403, 404, 409, 422, 503, Idempotency Idempotency-Key header.
proposed: Declare the request with the case reference and the matched_to value of LOV-MATCH plus the Idempotency-Key header, and record every further element as unspecified rather than inventing it.

title: The legacy word a broker has no value in LOV-PROCEEDS-SRC
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md, RWB-E4-044 AC1; TSD P8 T3.2
section: s7 Acceptance criteria AC1; s8 Business rules
description: Legacy AC1 says money arrives from an auction, a broker or the LED, while LOV-PROCEEDS-SRC carries CUSTOMER, LED, AUCTION, BUYER, AGENCY, INSURER and GUARANTOR and has no broker value, so the list value that a broker receipt takes is not specified.
evidence: TSD P8 T3.2 LOV-PROCEEDS-SRC: CUSTOMER, LED, AUCTION, BUYER, AGENCY, INSURER, GUARANTOR. Legacy AC1: matches money from an auction, a broker or the LED to the right case.
proposed: Read the legacy word a broker as the AGENCY value of LOV-PROCEEDS-SRC, add no list value, and confirm the reading with the reference-data owner when the list version in force is published.

title: payment_match_rule is defined in the TSD P8 data model but has no owner in the Ownership Map
source: TSD P8 Payments and posting v2 T3.1; _work/msr/plan/ownership.json tables
description: The TSD P8 data model introduces payment_match_rule with thirteen fields and the match type, tolerance, window and grace values, but the Ownership Map carries no row for it and gives P8 the proceeds table only, so neither the table owner nor the contract that publishes the version in force is specified.
evidence: TSD P8 T3.1 payment_match_rule DF-REF-261 to DF-REF-273; ownership.json tables has proceeds with owner P8 and no payment_match_rule entry.
proposed: Read the match rules as governed rule rows of rwb-decision, read the version in force on its contract, and do not declare payment_match_rule as a table of this service until the map gives it an owner.

title: The name of the JOB-07 event-started workflow is not published
source: Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 44 JOB-07; Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1
description: Slide 44 gives JOB-07 as an event-triggered workflow owned by rwb-payment and the design names its matchPayments activity, but no source gives the workflow a name, so the workflow element of the contract cannot be named from a source.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 44: JOB-07 Payment matching, Airflow: ACE data ready, rwb-payment, event-triggered workflow. Temporal and Drools design: rwb-payment matchPayments activity (JOB-07, started by AceDataReady).
proposed: Carry the workflow as the JOB-07 event-started workflow with the placeholder, and fix only its input and signal elements so that the history is stable when the name is confirmed.

title: The split plan carries no requirement id for this slice
source: _work/msr/plan/split_plan.json RWB-P8-E4044-APP and RWB-P8-E4044-CON; FSD P8 A2.4
description: Both slices of RWB-E4-044 carry an empty requirement list while the FSD keeps the feature as FEAT-PAY-04 with its rules VR-P8-004-1 and BR-P8-004, so no requirement id can be cited for the traceability row.
evidence: split_plan.json reqs empty for RWB-P8-E4044-APP and RWB-P8-E4044-CON; FSD P8 A2.4 FEAT-PAY-04.
proposed: Trace the slice to FEAT-PAY-04, VR-P8-004-1 and BR-P8-004 until a requirement id is allocated, and cite the placeholder in the traceability row.

title: The payload elements of the three payment events are not published
source: Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 42 and 43; TSD P8 Payments and posting v2 T5.3
section: s12.3 Events published; s12.4 Events consumed
description: The event catalogue and the TSD name TreatmentBooked, PaymentMissed and ProceedsMatched and their topic, and the catalogue notes give CloudEvents on Kafka keyed on the case, but no AsyncAPI document or element list of the three payloads is in the sources, so the event schema cannot be written from a source alone.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 17 OUT: topic rwb.payment.events.v1: TreatmentBooked, PaymentMissed, ProceedsMatched. Slide 42 notes: CloudEvents on Kafka, key caseId, schemas versioned with BACKWARD compatibility. TSD P8 T5.3 lists the three events with direction only.
proposed: Declare the three schemas with the CloudEvents 1.0 envelope, the event id, the case key and the identifiers each event names, and carry every further element as the placeholder until the event owner publishes the AsyncAPI document.

title: The acceptance criteria and test cases of RWB-E4-048 are generic placeholders that name no rental value
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (heading RWB-E4-048); FSD P8 Payments and posting v3 A2.9
section: A2.9 Run the deed in lieu rental auto-debit, acceptance criteria and test cases
description: Both legacy criteria and all four legacy test cases are placeholder text. AC1 says the data and the rule version are in place, the trigger arrives and the rental is taken by auto-debit; AC2 says the decision log cannot be written and the user sees MSG-P7-003. Neither line names a rental amount, a debit day, an account, a window or an arrears limit, so the target criteria can assert only the shape and the flow and not a business value.
evidence: Legacy master lines 14234 to 14244 (criteria) and 14285 to 14290 (test cases); FSD P8 A2.9.4.1 AC-P8-009-01 is the same one-line placeholder
proposed: Keep both criteria and the four test case IDs verbatim on the app story with the origin tag and read them against the target flow, and ask the business analyst to replace the placeholder with named values in a later version of the legacy master

title: No source gives the rental amount, the debit day or the arrears threshold of the deed in lieu rental
source: FSD P8 A2.9; FSD S2 TDR, settlement and deed in lieu v3 A2.16; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 (R-DIL-32, R-DIL-34, R-DIS-63); TSD P8 v2 T3.1 and T3.2
section: A2.9.3.1 business rules; TSD P8 T3.1 proceeds
description: The rental of a deed in lieu buy-back needs an amount, a debit day and an arrears threshold. The rules name the steps and not the values: R-DIL-32 creates the rental record and sets the auto-debit, R-DIL-34 hands the asset to disposal when the rental arrears exceed the limit, and R-DIS-63 names a threshold, but no file states any of the three values. TSD P8 T3.1 gives proceeds.amount only as a number received from the core bank, and the rental terms live in rwb-treatment, which publishes no field list for them.
evidence: FSD S2 A2.16.3.1 rule R-DIL-32; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-DIL-32, R-DIL-34, R-DIS-63 and the deed in lieu route summary; TSD P8 T3.1 DF-FIN-001 to DF-FIN-009
proposed: Read the amount, the debit day and the arrears threshold from the rwb-treatment rental terms and from reference data in force, keep all three out of the code, and confirm the value set with the business owner before the wave 3 test entry

title: The rental terms arrive through the rwb-treatment contract, which the plan does not carry as a contract dependency, and the field list of that answer is not published
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 18 (rwb-treatment OUT); Ownership Map (treatment owner S2); Work Package B-P8-01 slice RWB-P8-E4048-APP (contract dependencies empty)
section: Section 3 preconditions; section 12.2 REST operations consumed
description: The rental terms of the deed in lieu agreement are rwb-treatment data, so the app story reads them through the treatment contract and holds no treatment table. The slice carries no contract dependency for that read, and no source publishes the field list of the rental part of the treatment answer, so the story names the consumed element, declares it faked and marks the field names as not specified.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 18 rwb-treatment OUT (treatment, contract, deed-in-lieu agreement); Ownership Map treatment owner S2; TSD P8 T5.2 lists only the monolith Java interfaces; the slice JSON has empty contract dependencies
proposed: Treat the treatment read as a class C dependency built against its fake, add the row at the next plan refresh, and settle the rental-terms field names with the rwb-treatment owner before the build starts

title: The test cases of RWB-E4-048 are generic placeholders and name no contract element
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (heading RWB-E4-048); FSD P8 A2.9.4
description: The four legacy test cases are one-line placeholders (run the rental auto-debit, not recorded, a role without the right, a forced decision log failure) and name no operation, field, list value or event. They prove the behaviour of the app story and cannot test the contract artefact, so the contract slice keeps the legacy IDs with the app story and adds its own contract cases.
evidence: Legacy master lines 14285 to 14290: TC-E4-048-01 to TC-E4-048-04
proposed: Keep the four legacy test case IDs on the app story and test the contract with new contract-level cases that assert the document, the schemas, the event envelope and the DDL template

title: No source gives a rental-specific property or a separate receipt and arrears operation, and the consumed rental-terms element has no field list
source: TSD P8 v2 T3.1, T3.2 and T-A.1; API Specification v4 (Proceeds, MatchRequest, ProceedsPage); Architecture v5 slide 17 (rwb-payment IN)
section: Section 7 criteria AC3 and AC4; section 11 data; section 12.2
description: The receipt and the arrears follow-up have no shape of their own in any source: proceeds carries source, amount, received_date and matched_to and nothing about a rental period, an installment schedule, a debit day or an arrears threshold. The IN row of the slide names the allocate path for the manual match and the TSD names only the list and the match, so no operation issues a receipt or follows up arrears as a separate call. The contract therefore models both as proceeds rows of the one match resource and marks the rental-terms element of rwb-treatment as not specified.
evidence: TSD P8 T3.1 DF-FIN-001 to DF-FIN-009; TSD P8 T3.2 LOV-PROCEEDS-SRC and LOV-MATCH; TSD P8 T-A.1 API-P8-001 and API-P8-002; API Specification v4 Proceeds and MatchRequest
proposed: Declare the rental receipt and the arrears follow-up as Proceeds instances distinguished by source and matched_to, add no rental property, and confirm with the business owner whether a rental period belongs on proceeds or on the treatment terms

title: The name of the rental collection workflow and the package code that decides the arrears threshold are not specified
source: Architecture v5 slide 17 (activities matchPayments, confirmBookings, postProceeds) and slide 44 (JOB-07, JOB-08); Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slides 13, 14 and 18
section: Section 12.5 workflows and activities; section 18 rules
description: The design names the three activities and the mechanism (an event-started workflow on the owning queue) but not the workflow that hosts them, and it names the R-DIL rows as treatment-stage rules, so the package code that holds the arrears threshold for the payment step has no name in any file.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 17 TMP rows; Ownership Map JOB-07 and JOB-08 (mechanism event-triggered workflow, no workflow name); Temporal and Drools Design slide 18 (R-DIL rules in rwb-treatment)
proposed: Fix the workflow name as a local design choice in the baseline, and read the arrears threshold from the package version in force announced on RulePackageInForce until rwb-decision names the package code
